L181:     CONSUMER PRICE INDEX - OCTOBER 2026
L182:     The Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U) increased 0.4 percent on a seasonally adjusted basis in October
L183:     after rising 0.6 percent in September, the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported today.
L184: 
L185:     The index for shelter rose 0.3 percent in October, accounting for over thirty percent of the monthly all items increase.
L186:     The food index increased 0.5 percent in October, as the food at home index rose 0.4 percent and the food away from home
L187:     index increased 0.5 percent. The index for energy increased 0.7 percent over the month following a 5.2-percent increase
L188:     in September.
L189: 
L190:     The index for all items less food and energy rose 0.3 percent in October, as it did in September and August. Indexes that
L191:     increased over the month include recreation, medical care, motor vehicle insurance, household furnishings and operations,
L192:     and education. Conversely, the index for used cars and trucks and the index for communication were among the small number
L193:     of major indexes that decreased in October.
L194:

L200:     October 2026 for indexes where October 2025 data are unavailable. Information about handling missing data is

L190: # Household Debt Increased Moderately; Delinquency Transition Rates Remain Flat
L191: 
L192: November 10, 2026
L193: NEW YORK—The Federal Reserve Bank of New York’s Center for Microeconomic Data today issued its 【150†Quarterly Report on Household Debt and Credit】 . The report shows total household debt expanded by $334 billion, a 1.8% increase, in Q3 2026, to $19.1 trillion. The report is based on data from the New York Fed’s nationally representative 【151†Consumer Credit Panel】 . It includes a one-page summary of key takeaways and their supporting data points.
L194: The New York Fed also issued an accompanying 【97†Liberty Street Economics†libertystreeteconomics.newyorkfed.org】 blog post examining differences in the rise in credit card delinquencies by neighborhood income and the role of changing lending standards over the last several years.
L195: “Household debt levels rose moderately, led by increases in mortgage and home equity line of credit originations” said Donghoon Lee, Economic Research Advisor at the New York Fed. “Although delinquency transition rates for housing debts have crept up, the overall credit quality of these loans remains strong.”
L196: Mortgage balances rose by $257 billion in the third quarter and totaled $13.4 trillion at the end of September. Home equity lines of credit (HELOC) balances rose by $23 billion totaling $481 billion, the largest increase in HELOC balances observed since 2005. Credit card balances rose by $22 billion and stood at $1.29 trillion, and auto loan balances increased by $21 billion to $1.73 trillion. Student loan balances edged up by $5 billion and stood at $1.66 trillion.
L197: The pace of mortgage originations grew notably with $595 billion newly originated in Q3 2026. Auto loan originations remained at a high rate; there were $208 billion in new auto loans appearing on credit reports during the third quarter. Aggregate limits on credit cards continued to rise, with a $115 billion uptick in the third quarter. HELOC limits rose by $31 billion, continuing an expansion in HELOCs that began in 2022.
L198: Aggregate delinquency rates worsened in Q3 2026, with 5.0% of outstanding debt in some stage of delinquency, up 0.3 percentage points from the previous quarter. Transition into early delinquency continued to tick up for auto loans and mortgages but improved slightly for credit cards. Transition rates into serious delinquency slightly improved for credit cards and student loans, while those for auto loans and HELOCs remained flat.
L199: For mortgages, the transition rate into serious delinquency worsened but remains low by historical standards.

L150: ## VIX Strategies
L151: 
L152: VIX futures and options have unique characteristics and behave differently than other financial-based commodity or equity products. Understanding these traits and their implications is important. VIX futures and options may provide market participants with flexibility to hedge a portfolio, employ strategies in an effort to generate returns from relative pricing differences, or express a bullish, bearish or neutral outlook for broad market implied volatility.
L153: ### Portfolio Hedging
L154: 
L155: One of the biggest risks to an equity portfolio is a broad market decline. The VIX Index has had a historically strong inverse relationship with the S&P 500^{®} Index. Consequently, a long exposure to volatility may offset an adverse impact of falling stock prices. Market participants should consider the time frame and characteristics associated with VIX futures and options to determine the utility of such a hedge.
